summary: The focused entity-preserving parse mode requires harness maintenance. The old harness always uses the default constructor, so it cannot exercise processEntities=false in either source version.

claims.necessity_reason: XMLDocument supports processEntities=false, and XMLText::ParseDeep uses it to retain entities. A finite input such as & exercises that mode only when the document is constructed with false. The complete old harness always constructs XMLDocument without arguments and has no equivalent route.

before.requirement: Parse XML text containing a recognized entity with processEntities=false, retaining the entity in the text value.
before.reason: The constructor defaults processEntities to true, while the harness always uses that default.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The text mode selected when entity processing is disabled omits the entity-processing flag.
With entity processing enabled, reading a recognized amp entity converts it to an ampersand.
The selected change group concerns cleanup of parsed nodes.

after.requirement: Parse XML text containing a recognized entity with processEntities=false, retaining the entity in the text value.
after.reason: The constructor and text parser still support the mode, but the same old harness still uses the true default.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The text mode selected when entity processing is disabled omits the entity-processing flag.
With entity processing enabled, reading a recognized amp entity converts it to an ampersand.
The changed destructor cleans up parsed nodes.

claims.comparison_reason: Both source versions support the same constructor setting. On both sides, the complete old entry point supplies no constructor argument or other way to disable entity processing.
